input.command: ls -R src | head -50; cat -n src/store.ts; cat -n src/routes.ts
grep -rn "system\|isAdmin\|deleteRepo" --include=*.ts --include=*.md --include=*.json . | grep -v node_modules | head -30; ls -a; git log --oneline | head

input.reason: In src/store.ts, Store.deleteRepo runs an unconditional delete only when ctx.isAdmin is true. For everyone else it runs line 29: `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')`. The `OR owner = 'system'` clause means a non-admin's delete also matches any repo owned by 'system', not just the caller's own repos. The route handler in src/routes.ts (deleteRepo, line 28) passes req.params.id and req.user straight to store.deleteRepo and does no ownership check of its own. I searched the tree for other guards and found none: nothing else references 'system' or isAdmin, there are no tests, and there is no middleware that limits this route to admins. The only admin-style check in routes.ts is isAdminAddress, and it applies only to auditLog. Both findings describe this same defect, one at the call site and one at the SQL filter.
input.failure_scenario: A repo row exists with id 'shared-infra' and owner 'system'. Any logged-in non-admin user (for example oid 'alice', isAdmin false) calls the deleteRepo route with params.id = 'shared-infra'. The route calls Store.deleteRepo, which runs `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = 'shared-infra' AND (owner = 'alice' OR owner = 'system')`. The row matches the owner = 'system' branch, so the delete succeeds and returns 204. A shared system repository is gone for every user.
input.severity_reason: This is an authorization bypass that any authenticated user can trigger with one request. It permanently deletes shared, system-owned repository records, which is data loss affecting all users. The attacker only needs the repo id, and no admin rights or unusual state are required.
